artists.name: Burna Boy
artists.bio: Port Harcourt's Damini Ogulu turned Afro-fusion into a stadium language: muscular live shows, restless albums and a voice that can make triumph sound like testimony.

songs.title: Own It (feat. Ed Sheeran & Burna Boy)

artists.name: Tems
artists.bio: Tems never sanded down her grainy, low-slung voice for pop. Pop moved toward her instead, making the Lagos songwriter a rare star whose restraint carries as much force as a chorus.

artists.name: Rema
artists.bio: Rema treats Afrobeats as a moving target. From the bright immediacy of Calm Down to the darker pulse of HEIS, he keeps expanding the sound without losing his Benin City fingerprints.

artists.name: Tyla
artists.bio: Johannesburg's Tyla turned popiano from a smart description into a global pop format. Her light vocal touch, dance language and precision make difficult crossover work look effortless.

songs.title: SHE DID IT AGAIN (feat. Zara Larsson)
Talk to Me (feat. Tyla, Nile Rodgers)

artists.name: Wizkid
artists.bio: Wizkid's understated cool became a global template. A deep catalogue, the long afterlife of Essence and his gift for melodic economy keep Starboy present in every new Afrobeats conversation.

songs.title: Boom (feat. MOTi, Ty Dolla $ign, Wizkid & Kranium)
My Love (feat. Major Lazer, WizKid, Dua Lipa) - Spotify Single Version
Soco (feat. Wizkid, Ceeza Milli, Spotless & Terri)

artists.name: Ayra Starr
artists.bio: Ayra Starr pairs diary-page candour with arena ambition. Her voice can sound bruised, defiant and playful in one record, giving the Mavin star a reach far beyond any one trend.

songs.title: Love Don't Cost A Dime - Re-Up

artists.name: Davido
artists.bio: Davido built longevity on urgency: huge hooks, generous collaborations and the feeling that every release is a public event. Few artists turn fan energy into commercial force as reliably.

songs.title: Hayya Hayya (Better Together) - Music from the FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022 Official Soundtrack

artists.name: Asake
artists.bio: Asake compressed Fuji phrasing, massed vocals and amapiano log drums into a instantly recognisable rush. His catalogue moves like a crowd even when the subject turns inward.

artists.name: OMAH LAY
artists.bio: Omah Lay made interior monologue commercially huge. His wounded melodies, soft-spoken writing and shadowy production created a modern Afrobeats lane that many artists now borrow from.

artists.name: CKay
artists.bio: CKay's Love Nwantiti became one of the genre's defining digital exports, but his larger signature is emotional economy: intimate writing, simple melodies and records built to travel.

songs.title: love nwantiti (feat. Dj Yo! & AX'EL) - Remix
love nwantiti (feat. ElGrande Toto) - North African Remix
love nwantiti (ah ah ah) [feat. Joeboy & Kuami Eugene] [Remix]

artists.name: Fireboy DML
artists.bio: Fireboy writes romance with the eye of a short-story author. Peru widened the audience, while his albums show the quieter craft: clean melodies, emotional detail and unusual consistency.

artists.name: Victony
artists.bio: Victony's elastic voice can glide through street-pop, R&B and experimental production without losing its identity. His feature run turned promise into one of the scene's most adaptable profiles.

artists.name: MOLIY
artists.bio: Accra-born MOLIY makes dance music with a sly edge. Her airy delivery and diaspora-minded collaborations have carried Ghanaian pop into clubs and charts far outside its home market.

songs.title: SAD GIRLZ LUV MONEY Remix (feat. Kali Uchis and Moliy)
SHAKE IT TO THE MAX (FLY) - REMIX
SAD GIRLZ LUV MONEY Remix (feat. Kali Uchis and Moliy) - Slowed + Reverb
What I Like (with Moliy, Ayetian, & Tyga)
Shake It To The Max (Done With Ya Ex)
Shake It To The Max (FLY) - Kalash & Maureen Remix
Shake It To The Max - Tuff Remix
SAD GIRLZ LUV MONEY (feat. Moliy & Kali Uchis) - Vigro Deep Amapiano Remix

artists.name: BNXN
artists.bio: BNXN's husky tone gives features instant shape, but the catalogue proves he is more than a hook specialist. He writes with humour, vulnerability and a traveller's ear for rhythm.

artists.name: Seyi Vibez
artists.bio: Seyi Vibez turns prayer, survival and street testimony into hypnotic music. His prolific run built a loyal audience that hears spiritual weight beneath the raw vocal grain.

songs.title: Big Big Things (feat. Kizz Daniel & Seyi Vibez)

artists.name: FOLA
artists.bio: FOLA's rise rests on melodic instinct rather than noise. He writes compact, emotionally direct songs and has quickly become one of the voices most likely to own the next chorus.

artists.name: Ruger
artists.bio: Ruger blends dancehall swing with a teasing pop persona and unusually clean songwriting. Beneath the swagger is a sharp ear for hooks that survive after the viral moment passes.

artists.name: Mavo
artists.bio: Mavo arrived with the velocity of internet culture: clipped phrases, quick melodic turns and records built for replay. The next test is turning that heat into a durable body of work.

artists.name: Odeal
artists.bio: Odeal connects London intimacy with Nigerian rhythm. His warm, conversational vocals make his songs feel close-up, while patient arrangements give them room to travel.

artists.name: Kizz Daniel
artists.bio: Kizz Daniel has spent a decade making difficult pop mechanics feel obvious. He understands the exact phrase, pause and melodic turn that transforms a good idea into a continental earworm.

songs.title: Big Big Things (feat. Kizz Daniel & Seyi Vibez)

artists.name: Olamide
artists.bio: Olamide is both a street-rap institution and an ecosystem builder. His own catalogue maps Lagos slang and ambition; YBNL multiplied that influence through a generation of major voices.

artists.name: ODUMODUBLVCK
artists.bio: ODUMODUBLVCK raps like a collision is about to happen. The Abuja artist mixes Nigerian cadence, grime weight and football-sized chants into a presence that feels larger than the track.

songs.title: BLOOD ON THE DANCE FLOOR (feat. Bloody Civilian and Wale)
DOG EAT DOG II (feat. Cruel Santino and Bella Shmurda)

artists.name: Sarz
artists.bio: Sarz builds drums with personality. His fingerprints run through multiple Afrobeats eras, and his producer-led projects prove an architect can hold the centre without becoming the vocalist.

artists.name: Amaarae
artists.bio: Amaarae makes pop that refuses a fixed passport or genre. The Ghanaian-American auteur folds highlife, rap, club music and fashion into albums that reward curiosity as much as immediacy.

songs.title: SAD GIRLZ LUV MONEY Remix (feat. Kali Uchis and Moliy)
In The Night (feat. Jorja Smith & Amaarae)
SAD GIRLZ LUV MONEY Remix (feat. Kali Uchis and Moliy) - Slowed + Reverb

artists.name: Young Jonn
artists.bio: Young Jonn moved from the producer tag to the centre of the record without losing his hitmaking instinct. His compact melodies still carry the efficiency of someone who understands every layer.

songs.title: Big Big Things (feat. Kizz Daniel & Seyi Vibez)

artists.name: Adekunle Gold
artists.bio: Adekunle Gold's career is a study in reinvention: folk-rooted beginnings, highlife colour and increasingly polished global pop. The through-line is careful writing and unmistakable warmth.

songs.title: PAMI (feat. Wizkid, Adekunle Gold & Omah Lay)
D O D O - Adekunle Gold Version

artists.name: Shallipopi
artists.bio: Shallipopi turns Benin City slang, deadpan humour and spare production into sticky street-pop. His cultural impact lives as much in everyday language as it does in streaming totals.

artists.name: Oxlade
artists.bio: Oxlade's falsetto is recognisable within seconds. KU LO SA gave it global scale, while his best records use that high register as texture rather than a trick.

songs.title: KU LO SA - A COLORS SHOW

artists.name: FAVE
artists.bio: FAVE's smoky voice carries both calm and tension. Her songwriting favours uncluttered emotional scenes, giving every feature and solo record an immediate point of view.

artists.name: Joeboy
artists.bio: Joeboy helped define the soft, romantic side of the streaming-era breakthrough. His easy delivery disguises disciplined pop writing and a catalogue built for repeat listening.

songs.title: love nwantiti (ah ah ah) [feat. Joeboy & Kuami Eugene] [Remix]

artists.name: Tiwa Savage
artists.bio: Tiwa Savage brought elite R&B control into Nigerian pop and kept evolving after the first crossover wave. Her longevity rests on vocal precision, stage craft and fearless collaboration.

artists.name: Lojay
artists.bio: Lojay writes desire in close detail and sings it with a grainy, instantly identifiable tone. Monalisa opened the door; his darker, more intricate records explain why it stayed open.

songs.title: Mnike (Remix) (feat. DJ Maphorisa, Shallipopi, Lojay, Ceeka RSA, Tyrone Dee & Nandipha808)

artists.name: JAZZWRLD
artists.bio: JAZZWRLD brings a soulful, composer-led sensibility to amapiano. His growing catalogue favours atmosphere and patient musical development over disposable dance-floor formulas.

songs.title: Isaka II (6am) [with Tems, Omah Lay, Thukuthela, JAZZWRLD, Lekaa Beats]
I Know Who I Be (with JAZZWRLD & GL_Ceejay)
Vele Uyena (Risk It All) (feat. Elaine, JAZZWRLD, Thukuthela & Solaariss)

artists.name: Darkoo
artists.bio: Darkoo moves naturally between London rap cadence and West African melody. That bilingual musical instinct makes each collaboration feel like a bridge rather than a marketing exercise.

songs.title: Body (Remix) [feat. ArrDee, E1 (3x3), ZT (3x3), Bugzy Malone, Buni, Fivio Foreign & Darkoo]
Focus On Me (All The Sexy Girls In The Club)

artists.name: Black Sherif
artists.bio: Black Sherif sings as if every line costs something. His cracked, urgent voice turns migration, pressure and ambition into anthems that connect Accra street reality with a global audience.

artists.name: CIZA
artists.bio: CIZA represents amapiano's fast-moving new school: youthful vocals, bright Bacardi energy and an instinct for dance moments that can travel across borders before radio catches up.

songs.title: Isaka II (6am) [with Tems, Omah Lay, Thukuthela, JAZZWRLD, Lekaa Beats]
Carolina (feat. Major League DJz and Abidoza)
Isaka (6am) Frank Delour Mix - In Miami

artists.name: Shoday
artists.bio: Shoday balances street-pop directness with a romantic melodic touch. His rise reflects a new discovery pipeline where consistency after the viral spark matters more than industry permission.

artists.name: King Promise
artists.bio: King Promise's smooth baritone is built for patience, not spectacle. He carries Ghanaian highlife ease into modern Afropop and has become one of the continent's most dependable collaborators.

songs.title: Can't Let You Go (feat. King Promise)

artists.name: Zlatan
artists.bio: Zlatan converts street language and dance into pop momentum. Zanku was a full cultural moment, and his continued relevance comes from knowing when to lead and when to energise a feature.

artists.name: Bella Shmurda
artists.bio: Bella Shmurda sings with an exposed edge that makes hustle records feel personal. His melodies carry the tension between celebration and survival at the heart of Lagos street-pop.

songs.title: DOG EAT DOG II (feat. Cruel Santino and Bella Shmurda)

artists.name: Blaqbonez
artists.bio: Blaqbonez pairs technical range with an internet-native sense of theatre. The jokes draw attention, but the reason he stays is musical flexibility and a clear understanding of character.

songs.title: W For Wetego (feat. Young Jonn, Phyno & DJ 808)

artists.name: Khaid
artists.bio: Khaid's compact melodies and unpolished emotional tone made him a fast streaming-era breakout. His records work best when vulnerability interrupts the confidence.

artists.name: Chike
artists.bio: Chike brings an actor's sense of pacing to love songs. His clear diction and patient arrangements have made him a dependable voice for romance without chasing every rhythmic trend.

artists.name: Diamond Platnumz
artists.bio: Diamond Platnumz turned Bongo Flava stardom into a regional business system. His catalogue, visual scale and Wasafi platform keep East Africa central to the continental pop map.

songs.title: Wasted Energy (feat. Kaash Paige & Diamond Platnumz) - Remix

artists.name: Tekno
artists.bio: Tekno's sparse productions and spring-loaded melodies helped shape the mid-2010s Afropop boom. Even when releases slow, his writing and production DNA remain audible across the scene.

artists.name: Focalistic
artists.bio: Focalistic gave amapiano a rapper's narrative centre. His Pretoria slang, agile flow and cross-border collaborations helped the sound speak beyond the dance floor.

songs.title: Dlala Ka Yona (feat. Focalistic, Ricky Lenyora, Uncool MC & Mellow & Sleazy)
Tobetsa Remake (feat. Focalistic, Daliwonga & ShaunMusiq & Ftears)

artists.name: Uncle Waffles
artists.bio: Uncle Waffles made the DJ booth feel like centre stage. Her high-energy sets, sharp visual identity and international touring turned curation itself into a headline performance.

songs.title: Wadibusa (feat. Royal MusiQ, OHP Sage, & Pcee)

artists.name: Phyno
artists.bio: Phyno proved indigenous-language rap could command the mainstream without translation. His authority comes from technical control, Eastern cultural detail and a catalogue that still pulls crowds.

songs.title: W For Wetego (feat. Young Jonn, Phyno & DJ 808)

artists.name: Shatta Wale
artists.bio: Shatta Wale is Ghanaian dancehall as public theatre: confrontational, prolific and impossible to ignore. His direct bond with fans gives the music an influence that raw platform numbers miss.

artists.name: Stonebwoy
artists.bio: Stonebwoy connects Ghanaian identity with reggae and dancehall craft. Years of touring and collaboration make him a steady continental ambassador rather than a one-cycle chart act.
